title: The Dual Width Invariant maxAntichainLen
content: maxAntichainLen is defined as the sup of antichain cardinalities (over allAntichains, the filtered powerset of the finite poset) — the transpose of the imported maxChainLen. antichain_card_le_maxAntichainLen records that every antichain is bounded by it (Finset.le_sup), and exists_antichain_card_eq_maxAntichainLen shows the bound is attained. Nonemptiness of the index set is free: the empty set is vacuously an antichain, so the sup is over a nonempty family. This dual invariant is the second factor in the product bound that follows.
mathContext: $\mathrm{maxAntichainLen} = \sup\{|A| : A \text{ an antichain}\}$, the order-theoretic dual of $\mathrm{maxChainLen}$.
prerequisites: Finset.sup and attainment of a finite sup

title: The Common Min–Max Counting Bound and Its Contrapositive
content: card_le_maxChainLen_mul_maxAntichainLen is the bridge inequality: Mirsky's mirsky_antichain_cover supplies ≤ maxChainLen antichains covering the poset, the universe injects into their union, and a calc chain bounds card ≤ Σ(antichain sizes) ≤ (number of antichains)·maxAntichainLen ≤ maxChainLen·maxAntichainLen (Finset.card_biUnion_le, Finset.sum_le_sum, Finset.sum_const). exists_long_chain_or_antichain is its contrapositive by by_contra/push_neg: if every chain ≤ r and every antichain ≤ s then maxChainLen ≤ r and maxAntichainLen ≤ s, so card ≤ r·s, contradicting r·s < card. This single dichotomy is the abstract Erdős–Szekeres, with all the hard content already in Mirsky.
mathContext: $|P| \le \mathrm{maxChainLen}\cdot\mathrm{maxAntichainLen}$; contrapositive: $rs < |P| \Rightarrow$ a chain of size $>r$ or an antichain of size $>s$.

title: The Dominance Order on Sequence Positions
content: SeqPos f is a one-field structure wrapping Fin N, equipped with the dominance partial order a ≤ b ↔ a.pos ≤ b.pos ∧ f a.pos ≤ f b.pos. Antisymmetry holds because equal positions force the points to coincide (SeqPos.ext on the position equality). Wrapping Fin N in a fresh structure is the key design move: it avoids any clash with Fin N's native linear order, so the dominance order can be installed as the PartialOrder instance. equivFin gives a Fintype borrowed from Fin N and card_eq : card (SeqPos f) = N; pos_injective records that the position map is injective — both needed to transport the dichotomy and preserve sizes.
mathContext: $a \preccurlyeq b \iff a_{\mathrm{pos}} \le b_{\mathrm{pos}} \wedge f(a_{\mathrm{pos}}) \le f(b_{\mathrm{pos}})$, a finite poset of cardinality $N$.

title: Chains ↔ Non-decreasing, Antichains ↔ Strictly Decreasing
content: The dictionary that makes the poset dichotomy mean something about sequences. image_pos_nondecr: the positions of a chain form a non-decreasing index set — comparable positions a, b with i ≤ j move the value the same way, and the boundary case where positions coincide is handled by antisymmetry. image_pos_strictdecr: the positions of an antichain form a strictly decreasing index set — for i < j the positions are unequal hence incomparable in the dominance order, and ¬(a ≤ b) unfolds (push_neg) to exactly f j < f i. card_image_pos preserves cardinalities via injectivity of the position map. So a 'long chain' becomes a long non-decreasing run and a 'long antichain' a long strictly-decreasing run.
mathContext: Chain $\Rightarrow$ $i \le j \Rightarrow f_i \le f_j$ (non-decreasing); antichain $\Rightarrow$ $i < j \Rightarrow f_j < f_i$ (strictly decreasing); sizes preserved.
prerequisites: chains and antichains in the dominance order

title: The Classical Erdős–Szekeres Theorem
content: erdos_szekeres_seq assembles the pieces: for f : Fin N → β over a linear order with r·s < N, apply the poset dichotomy to SeqPos f (whose cardinality is N by card_eq), then push the resulting chain or antichain through the position map using image_pos_nondecr / image_pos_strictdecr and card_image_pos. The conclusion is a non-decreasing run on > r positions or a strictly decreasing run on > s positions. Taking N = r·s + 1 recovers the classical 1935 statement that a sequence of r·s + 1 terms has a monotone subsequence of length r+1 (non-decreasing) or s+1 (strictly decreasing). The result holds over any LinearOrder codomain, not just the reals, and Erdős–Szekeres is absent from Mathlib, so the file fills a concrete gap.
mathContext: $rs < N \Rightarrow$ a non-decreasing run of length $>r$ or a strictly decreasing run of length $>s$; with $N = rs+1$, the classical theorem.
